@copilot Simplify the implementation in this existing PR and update this PR directly. Keep its current tracing behavior and compatibility; do not create a separate follow-up PR.

Apply these three reductions within instrumentation/akka/akka-http-10.0/javaagent:

1. Replace the hand-written ThreadLocal<ErrorInfo> lifecycle in AkkaHttpParsingErrorSingletons with the existing io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.api.internal.ScopedThreadValue<ErrorInfo>. Expose the holder through a zero-argument accessor and show the set/restore pairing directly in HttpServerControllerInstrumentation.IllegalRequestAdvice, carrying the previous value through @Advice.Enter and restoring on exceptional exits. Preserve marker consumption, clearing ambient state for unmarked entity-stream errors, consuming the current error before tracing, and restoring any outer value. Remove redundant enter/exit lifecycle wrappers.

2. Move malformedRequestTarget from src/test/scala/.../AbstractHttpServerInstrumentationTest.scala to one representative concrete baseline test class, AkkaHttpServerInstrumentationTest.scala. It currently repeats across four inherited server variants even though rejection occurs before the application handler. Retain the Java-route malformed-target regression so Akka HTTP 10.0 and 10.2 remain covered, including the exact HTTP 400 response, exactly one root server span, and existing attribute assertions. Keep the application-generated 400 and malformed-entity no-extra-span regressions.

3. Extract a small shared customizeResponse(context, response) helper in the existing AkkaHttpResponseMutator class for the duplicated customizer invocation and immutable-header application in AkkaFlowWrapper and AkkaHttpParsingErrorSingletons. Use the shared helper from both paths, preserving the returned response and instrumenter.end behavior. Avoid introducing a new helper class or broader abstraction.

Keep the MessageStartError marker and both controller hooks. Entity-stream failures share finishWithIllegalRequestError but already have a server span; emitErrorResponse provides the actual response after Akka's parsing-error handler. Keep Context.root(), shared HTTP instrumenter configuration, sampling, response customization, and no fabricated request attributes. Do not replace this with status-only tracing or otherwise broaden which responses are traced.

Follow repository guidance, apply the narrowest relevant formatting, and run targeted relevant tests. Scope is these simplifications, not unrelated fixes.

replies.body: Addressed in 96d1f4af. Replaced the lifecycle wrappers with explicit ScopedThreadValue set/restore in advice, moved the baseline regression to the concrete test class, and shared response customization through AkkaHttpResponseMutator. Marker consumption, exceptional restoration, actual-response tracing, and existing regressions are preserved. Focused baseline/preview tests, Java-route tests on Java 25 and 11, formatting, Checkstyle, and 30 Muzzle checks passed.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly to simplify parser-rejection tracing using the Pekko HTTP implementation as the model. For this feature, supporting Akka HTTP 10.2+ is sufficient. This supersedes the earlier request to retain both controller hooks and parser-rejection coverage on Akka HTTP 10.0. Do not create a separate follow-up PR.

Keep marking pre-delivery rejections through MessageStartError and its ErrorInfo VirtualField. Replace HttpServerControllerInstrumentation's finishWithIllegalRequestError/emitErrorResponse hooks with instrumentation around akka.http.ParsingErrorHandler.handle, following instrumentation/pekko/pekko-http-1.0/javaagent's ParsingErrorHandlerInstrumentation and PekkoHttpParsingErrorSingletons. The handler exists in Akka HTTP 10.2.0. Gate the new handler instrumentation on the handler class being present, and keep ordinary instrumentation working unchanged on older supported Akka HTTP versions. Do not raise the minimum version for the existing Akka HTTP instrumentation as a whole.

Remove the anonymous-controller class matching and ScopedThreadValue error propagation that the handler hook makes unnecessary. Start the rejection span before the parsing-error handler runs and end it on normal or exceptional exit so it covers response construction. Retain explicit Context.root() parenting rather than copying Pekko's Context.current(), since no incoming parent has been extracted. Preserve sampling and the shared HTTP instrumenter configuration, record the actual returned response status, and keep response customization with immutable-header application using the existing shared AkkaHttpResponseMutator helper. Do not fabricate unavailable request attributes. Preserve exception-safe scope cleanup if a current scope is used.

Only marked pre-delivery rejections should create these spans. Entity/response-stream failures after delivery already have a server span and must not get an extra one. Match the handler signature precisely and skip bridge/abstract methods as Pekko does, including custom Java or Scala handler implementations without double instrumentation.

Adjust the regression tests to the new feature boundary. On Akka HTTP 10.2+, retain raw-socket malformed-target coverage asserting the real HTTP 400 response and exactly one root SERVER span with the existing response-status-only attributes. Keep application-generated 400 and malformed-entity no-extra-span coverage. Older supported versions must continue to work without requiring parser-rejection spans; adapt the Java-route baseline coverage and any version-specific test configuration accordingly. Make only directly related documentation changes, if needed, to clarify this feature's version boundary.

Apply the narrowest relevant formatting and run focused tests covering the new handler path, duplicate-span prevention, and older-version compatibility. Keep the scope limited to this simplification.

replies.body: Implemented in 1f023b89. Rejection tracing now uses a gated Akka HTTP 10.2+ parsing-handler hook; the 10.0 baseline remains supported without parser-rejection spans. Focused baseline and 10.2 tests pass.

@copilot Add focused regression coverage for the handler-based rejection tracing now implemented in this existing PR. Update this PR directly, not a new PR. This is a scoped follow-up to the completed coding attempt and Copilot review 5644880332, finding https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20919#discussion_r4372107448.

The current Java-route malformed-request tests exercise only the default 400 response and discard response headers. Add installed-agent coverage on Akka HTTP 10.2+ using a configured custom ParsingErrorHandler that returns a different status. Send a raw malformed request, verify the actual returned status, and assert exactly one root SERVER span whose http.response.status_code matches that custom response. Retain the received response headers and assert X-Test-TraceId and X-Test-SpanId match the exported rejection span, proving that the customized immutable response is returned to the client. Follow existing repository and Pekko test patterns rather than adding unnecessary abstractions.

Keep the current behavior: class-gated ParsingErrorHandler instrumentation, MessageStartError marking, explicit Context.root(), sampling and shared HTTP instrumenter, no fabricated request attributes, and no duplicate spans for entity/response-stream failures after delivery. Preserve the existing default malformed-target, application-generated 400, and malformed-entity regression coverage and older-version instrumentation compatibility. Do not expand this into unrelated changes. Production changes are needed only if these focused tests expose an in-scope defect.

Apply the narrowest relevant formatting and run the focused tests covering the added custom handler/status/header assertions along with the existing related regressions.

replies.body: Added the custom 418 handler regression. The raw-socket test asserts the returned status, exactly one root server span with status 418, and response trace/span headers matching that span. Focused Java-route tests and formatting checks pass. Commit: `00f3235e`.

@copilot Replace the positional Object[] rejection-span state with a small typed AdviceScope in this existing Akka PR. Update this PR directly, not a separate PR. The user has accepted the scope-ownership suggestion in review 5645244504 and authorized this focused cleanup.

In AkkaHttpParsingErrorSingletons and ParsingErrorHandlerInstrumentation under instrumentation/akka/akka-http-10.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/akkahttp/v10_0/server, use a nullable, fully initialized AdviceScope with named Context, Scope, and ErrorInfo fields instead of Object[] and positional casts. Return null when no rejection span starts. Let the typed owner complete the operation, closing its scope before response customization and ending the instrumenter with the actual returned response and the original handler error. Update the enter/exit advice signatures and calls to use that type. Follow .github/instructions/javaagent.instructions.md's ownership convention and the existing Akka client AdviceScope pattern. Prefer a small nested class in an existing file over a new framework or extra bookkeeping abstraction.

Preserve current behavior: explicit Context.root() parenting, consuming the rejection marker before sampling/start, making the rejection span current during handler execution, restoring the enclosing context on normal and exceptional handler exits, shared response customization, nullable responses, actual response status, and no duplicate rejection spans for post-delivery failures. Keep the recently simplified customize-then-end sequence; do not reintroduce the removed response-customization try/finally or replacement catches. Keep the 10.2+ feature boundary, older-version instrumentation, and all existing regression coverage.

Do not modify Pekko or broaden this to failed-entry rollback infrastructure tracked by #20667. This cleanup improves type safety and explicit ownership but does not claim to solve failed-entry cleanup. Keep tests and unrelated code unchanged unless required by the typed signature change. Apply the narrowest relevant formatting and run the focused existing Java-route regression tests.

replies.body: Implemented in `100525ee`. Parser-handler advice now carries a nullable `AdviceScope` with named `Context`, `Scope`, and `ErrorInfo` fields; the scope owner closes, customizes the response, and ends the span. Focused Java-route tests and formatting checks pass.

@copilot Update this existing Akka PR directly so parser-rejection spans use Context.current() rather than Context.root(), matching the normal Akka HTTP server instrumentation. Do not create a separate PR. This user-directed decision supersedes our earlier requests to force root parenting. Modern server instrumentation preserves the supplied ambient context, including non-span values and server-span suppression; unavailable propagation headers alone do not justify resetting it.

In AkkaHttpParsingErrorSingletons.startSpan under instrumentation/akka/akka-http-10.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/akkahttp/v10_0/server, use Context.current() as parentContext for both shouldStart and start. Do not substitute a root fallback or bypass ordinary ambient server-span suppression. When no ambient parent exists the span will still naturally be a root span.

Keep the completed typed AdviceScope ownership cleanup and the rest of the implementation unchanged: marker consumption, making the started rejection span current during the handler, restoring the previous context on normal and exceptional exit, scope closure before completion, nullable responses, linear customize-then-end sequencing without reintroducing try/finally or catches, actual response status, sampling, and shared response customization. Preserve the 10.2+ feature boundary, older-version instrumentation, and prevention of extra rejection spans for post-delivery failures.

Update only directly affected source comments or test expectations that incorrectly require forced root parenting. Preserve the existing default/custom parsing-handler response-status and trace-header regressions, malformed-entity regression, and application-generated 400 regression. Keep this change narrow; do not add a new test suite or generic fixtures just for this parent-selection change. Apply the narrowest relevant formatting and run the focused existing Java-route regression tests.

Do not change Pekko or any other integration, and do not reopen closed Pekko PR #20961. Do not broaden this into a repository-wide parenting migration, removal of the rejection marker, response-customization hardening, or failed-entry rollback infrastructure tracked by #20667.

replies.body: Updated in `c68e7c67`: parser-rejection spans now use `Context.current()` for both `shouldStart` and `start`; the focused Java-route regression suite passes.
